content:
Nebraska remains the team to beat in NCAA Division I women's volleyball. The Huskers earned all 63 first-place votes in the Week 10 AVCA Coaches Poll, extending their winning streak to 23 matches after sweeping both Michigan and Michigan State on the road in straight sets. Nebraska now heads to Eugene for its toughest road test yet against No. 12 Oregon.

Pitt moved up to No. 2 behind Nebraska, riding a seven-match winning streak of its own. The Panthers swept Wake Forest and NC State over the past week, with Kentucky transfer Jordyn Dailey notching 22 blocks across four matches.

The latest NCAA.com Power 10, released November 2, also saw SMU rise while Tennessee fell to No. 10 after dropping two matches to Texas A&M and Missouri. Michigan State's 0-2 week did the most damage in the polls: the Spartans blew a 2-0 set lead against No. 19 Indiana before falling in five, then were swept by Nebraska, dropping out of the weekly poll entirely.

Elsewhere in the Big Ten, USC's playoff hopes took a heavy hit over Halloween weekend. After being swept by No. 1 Nebraska, the Trojans (9-13, 3-9 Big Ten) fell in four sets to No. 7 Wisconsin and were swept by No. 19 Minnesota, 25-19, 25-16, 25-23. USC is now winless in Big Ten matches at Galen Center and in danger of missing the NCAA Tournament for the first time since the 2021 season. The Trojans close their final true road trip at Maryland on Thursday and Rutgers on Saturday.

UCLA also fell to Wisconsin, dropping a straight-set decision 25-22, 25-17, 25-17 on November 1 at Pauley Pavilion. Wisconsin hit .354 with 45 kills and 14 blocks, led by Decelise Champion's match-high 15 kills and eight blocks and Eva Travis' 11 kills on .647 hitting.

In Tuesday night action around the country, Ohio swept Kent State 3-0, Toledo edged Bowling Green 3-2 in a five-set battle, and Florida State outlasted Georgia Tech 3-2 with a 21-19 fifth set.

Sources: NCAA.com; Just Women's Sports; Daily Trojan; California Sports Blog; ESPN via Sportswire Live.

title: Volleyball Week 10: Nebraska Unanimous No. 1 With 23 Straight Wins, Pitt Rises to No. 2, SMU Climbs as Tennessee Falls
